cover: Rule or judgment: a worksheet for any process

slides.title: Write the process down, step by step
slides.body: Do it with the person who does the job today. Include the exceptions they handle without thinking.

slides.title: Mark each step: rule or judgment
slides.body: A list of conditions is a rule. “It depends, you just have to read it” is judgment.

slides.title: Check the input on judgment steps
slides.body: Forms and spreadsheets rarely need a model. Free text, photos and documents might, often just to turn them into tidy fields.

slides.title: Circle the expensive mistakes
slides.body: A refund issued, a record deleted, an email sent to a patient. A circled step needs a person to approve it.

slides.title: Does the path change case by case?
slides.body: If each answer changes what you check next, an agent may fit. The same five steps with different data is automation.

slides.title: Read your sheet
slides.body: Rule steps are your automation. Judgment steps are where AI might help. Circled ones keep a person's final say.
